correctness.rationale: For finite chain rings valuation layers give B1=-1 and BB^T=-J modulo p; the two block equations give exact kernel, symmetry yields rowspace; every low valuation layer size is divisible by p so the code's restricted form is the high-coordinate dot product, giving hull one. Nonzero socle columns create weight-one vectors, dual valuation-layer differences create weight two, and the constant-column criterion gives all weight-one supports. All steps hold in characteristic two and mixed characteristic. Fourteen finite direct-ring multiplication tests independently confirm the restricted configurations.

originality.rationale: The strongest relevant original source arxiv:2610.08480 treats only the nilpotency-four prime-residue odd-prime graph and already has its dimension and one-dimensional hull; those are excluded from novelty. It reports distance two, whereas the new direct word gives distance one. Its conclusion proposes higher indices. The present statement supplies full rowspace/dual/hull and exact weight-one spectrum for every chain ring length >=3, including mixed characteristic; the other relevant real spectral and graph invariants do not imply these modular-code properties. Historical priority remains qualified.

value.rationale: The rowspace of the adjacency matrix is an intrinsic graph code. Uniform complete generator and parity-check models, precise dual and hull, and exact minimum-distance-one obstruction across all finite chain rings answer the motivating coding question with a structural result rather than an isolated small case. The all-length extension and explicit high-valuation weight-one support are mathematically reusable and identify why this natural code family has no single-error correction capability.
